turns.text: I'm on warfarin for a clot last year and my knees have been aching badly, especially on stairs at work. What can I take or do for the pain that's safe with warfarin?
Why is paracetamol the usual choice with warfarin? Does it affect the INR at all if I take it regularly?
How do topical gels compare with tablets for knee pain? Do they work well enough to be worth trying?
If I asked the anticoagulation clinic, what would they want to know before advising on pain relief?
What do physiotherapists usually recommend for aching knees in someone who's on their feet all day?
A friend at work uses a knee support and says it helped a lot. Is there anything to that, and what kind?
Someone else told me heat in the evening and ice after a long shift. Which is right, or both?
I'm a delivery driver and I can't afford time off to see the clinic. What can I do in the next couple of weeks on my own?
What signs would mean the knee pain is something I should get looked at rather than manage myself?
Can you write me a plan — paracetamol at normal doses, gel, exercises, supports, and what to raise at my next INR check?
